newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mongolian PM says no change in China ties.
newsitem.headline: Mongolian PM says no change in China ties.

text.p: Mongolian Prime Minister Mendsaikhany Enkhsaikhan said on Tuesday that the former communist nation's ties with its giant neighbour China will not change following the death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping.
"I don't see any major or immediate change of the relationship between Mongolia and China following Deng Xiaoping's death," Enkhsaikhan told a news conference.

Enkhsaikhan, 41, who heads Mongolia's newly elected coalition government, arrived in Tokyo last Saturday for an official five-day visit to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic ties between the two countries.
Enkhsaikhan said Japan was "the most important partner" for his country, which is wedged between China and Russia.

In Tuesday's news conference, Enkhsaikhan also called for further direct investment from Japan. He promised to carry out legal reforms in his country by June as part of an attempt to build infrastructure suitable for foreign investment.
In June, Mongolia will host an international conference, co-sponsored by the World Bank, to discuss foreign investment in its petroleum and copper, silver and gold sectors, he said.
During his stay, Enkhsaikhan also presented awards to individuals who promoted ties between the two countries, including one to popular Mongolian sumo wrestler Kyokushuzan.

"We have two ambassadors here in Japan, one at the embassy and the other, Kyokushuzan," Enkhsaikhan was quoted by Japanese government officials as telling Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Monday.
Kyokushuzan was promoted to the fourth-highest rank of "komusubi" for professional sumo's Spring Grand Tournament in Osaka next month.
